analysis.title: Charts on US Midterms
key_insights: Investors are increasingly focused on the US midterm election on November 3. Economic policy uncertainty has usually risen in August ahead of midterms.
S&P 500 volatility usually rises into midterm elections. The note says this has shown up lately, especially within the AI trade.
Across 13 midterm election years since 1985, the S&P 500 has a median return of 0% from the start of August through Election day. Returns have typically improved after the election.
Mutual funds and foreign investors have generally reduced demand for US equities ahead of midterms, then increased allocations afterwards.
GS prime brokerage data shows US equities were net sold in 4 of the past 5 weeks.
Polymarket shows 66% odds of a Democratic sweep and 27% for a Republican Senate with a Democratic House.
Equities have historically returned more under divided US government than under unified control.
Stocks have generally performed better in the second half of the 4-year presidential cycle than the first.
risk_factors: Election outcome uncertainty ahead of the November 3 midterms, with rising policy uncertainty and volatility.
Volatility in the AI trade into the election.
